title: airgap-dependency-curation-canary-upgrade-plan
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working draft playbook for preparing, validating, and executing air-gapped (fully offline) upgrades of Redwood Private deployments. Focus is on dependency curation (what to include in the bundle), an automated artifact seeding workflow, Terraform module notes for registry/ingress setup in offline environments, and a canary upgrade sequence that minimizes blast radius in regulated networks.

High-level goals:
- Produce a reproducible offline bundle (images, helm charts, tarballs, binaries, license files, checksum manifests).
- Provide a robust registry seeding flow that supports incremental updates and verifiable integrity.
- Define a canary upgrade path for clusters that allows fast rollback and automated validation hooks.
- Document Terraform interface expectations for offline registries / proxy resources.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not replace distro-specific packaging (RPM/DEB). It assumes customers want OCI images + tarballs + helm charts.

Assumptions:
- Customer will provide an internal OCI registry reachable from target clusters (Harbor/Quay/Artifactory supported).
- There is a secure transfer mechanism (sneakernet / vendor-provided staging host) to move bundles into the sealed network.
- KMS/HSM integration for signing manifests is optional; basic SHA256 checksums are required.

Bundle composition checklist (minimum viable offline bundle):
- manifest.yaml (bundle manifest with semantic version, datetime, included artifacts list).
- checksums.txt (SHA256 all artifacts + size + signing-key-id if applicable).
- images/ (tarred container image layers as OCI layout OR image.tar for each tagged image).
- charts/ (helm chart tgz files and index.yaml).
- binaries/ (kustomize, helm, redwoodctl, verify-signing script).
- k8s-manifests/ (operator CRDs, namespace manifests, rbac).
- tf-modules/ (compiled/templated terraform artifacts used for offline bootstrap; see notes below).
- upgrade-hooks/ (smoke-test scripts, postinstall validators).

Curation notes (what to exclude and why):
- Exclude development-only images (debug images, local-only build tags).
- Exclude images with external EULAs unless we have explicit redistribution rights. Mark these in manifest as LICENSE_PENDING.
- When multiple acceptable model serving images exist (quantized vs full fp16), include the smallest viable variant for initial seeding and a path to fetch heavier images later.

Artifact preparation commands (examples):
- Pull and save images as OCI layout (preferred):
  skopeo copy docker://registry/repo:tag oci:bundle/oci-layout:tag
- Export single-image tar (for registries that only accept docker load):
  docker pull registry/repo:tag && docker save registry/repo:tag -o images/repo-tag.tar
- Create checksums and sign (simple):
  sha256sum  images/* charts/* binaries/* > checksums.txt
  ./sign-manifest.sh checksums.txt > checksums.txt.sig

Registry seeding strategies (pick based on customer infra):
- push-from-staging-host: use a dedicated bastion inside sealed network to push images to the internal registry. Use regctl or crane for fast bulk imports.
- OCI layout file-system import: copy the OCI layout to a host that supports registry import tooling (Harbor/Quay offline import).
- Registry proxy-sync: for customers who have a local proxy cache (registry mirror), seed only the required image tags and configure mirror rules.

Terraform module notes (interfaces to expose to customers):
- Module: private_deploy_registry (inputs):
  - registry_endpoint (string)
  - registry_type (harbor|quay|artifactory)
  - tls_cert_id (optional)
  - initial_admin_user (string)
  - enable_namespace_scoping (bool)
- Module: airgap_ingress (inputs):
  - bastion_host_id
  - allowed_transfer_subnets (list of cidrs)
  - artifact_storage_bucket (string) # used for transient unpacking inside sealed network
- Outputs should be simple endpoints and credentials written to a secrets engine; module should NOT emit raw passwords into TF state without KMS encryption.

Terraform implementation notes:
- Keep provider versions pinned in the module root to avoid drift.
- Provide a helper script terraform-init-offline.sh that pre-downloads provider plugins and static modules as a .zip for import into airgapped workstation.
- Consider embedding a small provider mirror (replace provider registry addresses with local mirror) in the module docs.

Pre-upgrade validation checklist (run outside of upgrade window):
- Manifest integrity OK (checksums match + signatures valid).
- Registry reachable from each node in target cluster.
- Available disk capacity on nodes >= expected image delta + 20%. Use df -h and kubelet image garbage-collection thresholds.
- CRD compatibility: verify new CRDs do not conflict (diff current CRDs against new CRDs).
- Backup: take a snapshot of control plane manifests, PV data if stateful components are impacted.
- Have a rollback bundle prepared (previous release artifacts + checksums).

Canary upgrade plan (sequence):
1) Prepare canary namespace (redwood-canary) with minimal traffic.
2) Seed images and charts into local registry (only tags required for canary).
3) Deploy canary control plane components (stateless service + a single replica operator if applicable).
4) Run smoke tests (listed below). If tests pass for X=30m, continue. If tests fail, abort and roll back.
5) Gradually increase scope: more namespaces, scale replicas, then roll out cluster-wide.
6) Post-rollout validation window: 60m for core metrics (latency, error-rate, resource usage).

Smoke tests (can be automated via upgrade-hooks/):
- API surface sanity: call /health, /ready, /metrics endpoints for each component (should be 200 OK).
- End-to-end sample generation: feed a deterministic prompt with seed corpus and compare hashed outputs to expected baseline (allowing nondeterministic deltas to be flagged).
- KV cache warmup check: confirm caching warmed (cache hit ratio > configured baseline) after warmup phase.
- Resource check: observe pod restarts and OOMs (should be zero or expected limit).

Rollback plan (fast path):
- If canary fails: delete canary deployment and restore previous manifests from rollback bundle, re-seed previous images if necessary.
- If cluster-wide failure: trigger emergency rollback play (documented script that iterates through deployment list and re-applies previous image tags and helm charts).
- Communicate to SRE/Customer: standard incident drill with timeline and mitigations.

Monitoring and metrics to capture during upgrade:
- Token-level latency for inference endpoints (p50/p95/p99).
- CPU/GPU utilization and throttling events.
- Registry push/pull failure counts and latency.
- Disk pressure and image GC events.

Edge cases and troubleshooting notes:
- Corrupted OCI layout: compare checksums + re-import from original bundle.
- Registry auth failures: verify service account TTL and token clock skew vs KMS.
- Missing images at runtime: confirm imagePullSecrets are present; if using imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent and tag mutated, may need to force image update.
- Large model artifacts: for >100GB model blobs, consider splitting into chunked layers and providing a reassembly hook in redwoodctl.

Operational runbook snippets (copy/paste examples):
- Import images with regctl (on staging inside sealed net):
  regctl image import --oci /mnt/bundle/oci-layout --dest localhost:5000/repo --all
- Verify manifest checksums:
  sha256sum -c checksums.txt || echo "bundle integrity failed" && exit 1
- Automated canary deploy script pattern: (pseudo)
  ./redwoodctl deploy --namespace redwood-canary --chart charts/redwood-core-1.2.0.tgz --image-registry localhost:5000 --wait --timeout 900s

Open questions / TODOs (actionable):
- Decide on canonical signing approach: GPG vs KMS-signed attestations (SLSA). Need security input. (action: Priya)
- Finalize list of redistributable third-party images and mark the rest as "manual approval". (action: Liam)
- Add explicit terraform provider mirror recipe and publish terraform-init-offline.sh to repo. (action: Noah)

Appendix: quick upgrade timeline estimate (small cluster):
- Bundle prep + QA: 21 days (includes security and license checks).
- Transfer to sealed network: dependent on customer (hours to 2 days).
- Registry seeding + verification: 12 hours.
- Canary deploy + validation: 10 min watch + 60m validation window.
- Cluster-wide roll: rolling across nodes, expected 30m-2h depending on replica counts.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive in steps but lightweight in implementation detail to be adaptable to customer infra. I want feedback on the terraform module interface and whether we should include an optional operator-based registry-seeder component inside the sealed network.
- Please add any missing failure modes you have hit in customer installs.

End of draft."
